content:
We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts list. Need number of CH3 groups in the compound. Methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic, but also could be around 20-30 for CH3 attached to heteroatoms. In data we have peaks at 44.06, 34.54 (two), 26.90 (two), 26.18. Also aromatic carbons at 147,133.9,128.91 (two),127.68 (two). So aliphatic region: 44.06 likely a carbon attached to heteroatom (maybe CH2). 34.54 maybe CH2. 26.9 and 26.18 likely CH3? Typically methyl carbon ~ 10-30 ppm. So we have three peaks in that region: 26.90 (two signals maybe two equivalent methyls?), 26.18 (one). But 26.90 appears twice (maybe two distinct methyl groups with same shift). So total methyl carbons count: 3? Actually if two signals at 26.90 could be two distinct methyl groups with same shift, count 2. Plus one at 26.18 = 3 methyl groups. However need to verify if any other peaks could be methyl: 34.54 maybe CH3 attached to aromatic? Usually aromatic methyl ~ 20-25 ppm. 34 is higher, likely CH2. So answer likely 3.

But we could also cross-check with proton NMR to see methyl protons. Let's get proton NMR.
